Operating format

A working room for leaders making AI adoption real for people.

The session focuses on how AI changes daily work, management expectations, training, resistance, role design, and the talent plan leaders need for next year.

Stage 01

Workforce adoption briefing

The room

Where AI adoption becomes a workforce leadership issue.

The discussion asks how organizations help people use AI responsibly, redesign work around it, and respond honestly to fear, resistance, and capability gaps.

Audience
Executives and senior leaders accountable for people, operations, transformation, technology, learning, culture, risk, or workforce planning.
Access
Invitation-only, capped at nine executive participants for a moderated exchange rather than broadcast attendance.
Outcome
A clearer 2027 workforce adoption agenda that connects AI capability to roles, managers, skills, policies, and change leadership.
Moderated questions

The questions leaders need to answer before this topic becomes operational.

Each question is designed to expose the people systems required for AI adoption to survive beyond early adopters.

01

Where are employees actually adopting AI?

Which teams are using AI meaningfully today, which are pretending, which are avoiding it, and why?

02

Which roles will change first?

Where will AI reshape tasks, judgment, supervision, customer interaction, analysis, content, service, or management work fastest?

03

What should managers be expected to coach?

How should managers guide AI use, quality review, ethical boundaries, experimentation, and team-level workflow redesign?

04

How do we respond to fear and resistance?

What concerns are legitimate, what is misinformation, and how should leaders communicate without minimizing disruption?

05

What skills need to be built internally?

Which prompt, review, data, workflow, judgment, governance, and vendor-management capabilities should become core employee skills?

06

How should policies shape daily use?

What simple rules help employees know what is allowed, what is risky, when to disclose, and when to ask for help?

07

How does AI affect hiring and org design?

Which roles, teams, spans of control, job descriptions, career paths, and performance measures should change in 2027?

08

What workforce commitments belong in the 2027 operating model?

What training, change leadership, communications, manager enablement, and talent investments should executives commit to now?
